page: Amazon Web Services r8ib.metal-96xl is a dedicated bare-metal server tailored for extreme memory and compute demands within the memory-optimized family. Utilizing Intel x86_64 architecture, the instance provides direct hardware access to 192 physical cores and 384 vCPUs operating at a 3.9 GHz clock frequency. The architecture allocates 3072.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8.0 GB per-core ratio that addresses substantial RAM requirements without virtualization overhead.

The server does not include onboard local storage drives or discrete GPU acceleration hardware. Consequently, external network-attached storage must be provisioned to handle operating system installation, persistent database tables, and operational logs. To sustain data exchange across remote storage tiers and distributed clusters, the instance integrates a 400 Gbps baseline network interface, providing low-latency interconnectivity and broad data pipelines.

From a resource allocation standpoint, r8ib.metal-96xl provides high compute density alongside extensive memory capacity on a single physical host. The absence of hypervisor layers maximizes deterministic execution, though users must manage storage integration entirely over the network. The hardware profile is geared toward large-scale in-memory databases, substantial data caching arrays, real-time enterprise resource planning systems, and complex memory-bound analytics pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r8ib.metal-96xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized instance engineered for large-scale enterprise workloads requiring massive memory footprints and non-virtualized processing power. Powered by dedicated Intel x86_64 processors running at up to 3.9 GHz, the server delivers 192 physical cores and 384 vCPUs paired with 3072.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB per-core allocation. The platform does not bundle local disk storage or hardware GPU accelerators, necessitating network-attached storage architectures for persistent data management. High-volume communications are supported by a 400 Gbps baseline network bandwidth interface, facilitating rapid inter-node synchronization and distributed operations. Given its massive resource profile, r8ib.metal-96xl offers a consolidated environment for memory-bound tasks where virtualization overhead must be eliminated. The system is well fitted for enterprise in-memory databases like SAP HANA or Redis clusters, real-time telemetry processing, large electronic design automation jobs, and extensive memory-intensive computational analytics.
